items.title: George Avakian interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 21, 1998
items.q: he too was an enthusiast but he did it in a very organized way... Delaunay and Panassié worked very closely together

ctx.x: And you said this was about what year? What span?

‘37 to the summer of ‘39, the Fall of ‘37 when I went to Yale as a freshman. And in that period, Marshall wanted to cut back on some of his writing for magazines and so he let me take over part of his writing at Tempo Magazine, which was later taken over by Down Beat. So I did the Collector’s Corner and I got letters addressed to Professor Avakian, although I was only, well I guess I really started toward the end of my freshman year, and it kind of shocked me, because here I was an enthusiastic young collector…
It’s curious when you look at the music at that time, you were doing a jazz history, but the history of jazz wasn’t that old.
